title: Debugging Kotlin Programs knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Debugging Kotlin Programs”?
options: It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
questions.answer_key: Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Debugging Kotlin Programs”?
options: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Debugging Kotlin Programs”?
options: Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
Debugging Kotlin Programs removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.answer_key: Debugging Kotlin Programs removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Debugging Kotlin Programs removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
